output:
**What I found:** The rule is still declared, but it no longer applies to anything, so the gate needs its reach put back (the record calls this RESTORE). In `eslint.config.mjs:15-25`, a later `files: ['**/*.js']` block sets `no-restricted-syntax` again. In ESLint flat config, a later block replaces an earlier block's options for the same rule instead of adding to them. So every file, including `src/billing/invoice.js`, only gets the `DebuggerStatement` check, and the green runs were never checking for auth-internal imports.

**Why it matters:** Every PR since that second block went in has merged with no boundary check, so `invoice.js:1` may not be the only bypass. Billing also now depends on `signToken`, which only base64-encodes the claims (`src/auth/internal/token.js:2`). Anyone can forge an invoice link token, which is a security problem separate from the lint issue. If nothing changes, the rule stays decorative and more bypasses can merge.

**Do this first:**
1. In `eslint.config.mjs`, move the auth boundary off the shared rule key so the debugger block can't override it. Replace the first block's `rules` with:
   ```js
   'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { patterns: [{ group: ['**/auth/internal/**'],
     message: 'Import auth through src/auth/index.js, never its internals.' }] }],
   ```
   Then commit a known-bad file that imports `auth/internal`, and add a CI step that runs `eslint` on it with the full config and fails unless that message appears.
2. Restoring the rule makes `invoice.js:1` fail lint. Fix it in the same PR by giving `src/auth/index.js` a public export that billing can use. Whether auth should expose invoice tokens is the auth owner's decision. If that can't happen in this PR, add a one-entry baseline with an owner and an expiry date.
3. Give the token-forgery problem to the auth owner. `signToken` needs a real signature such as HMAC.

**What I did not check:**
- That the resolved config really drops the rule. I worked this out from flat-config semantics and didn't run anything: `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js`
- Whether other files already import auth internals: `npx eslint .` after the fix, or `rg "auth.internal" src --glob '!src/auth/**'`
- When the shadowing block was added. This isn't a git repo, so there's no history to look at.

```text
Gate:         eslint no-restricted-syntax auth-internal boundary (eslint.config.mjs:2-14), via `npm run lint`, merge-blocking on PRs
Stage:        PR CI (static analysis); unplaced pre-commit
Trigger:      narrowed — passed while a known-bad input (src/billing/invoice.js:1) existed
Proof:        UNPROVEN — no negative control; no recorded red run
Scope:        declared src/**/*.js minus src/auth/** / effective none (block 2 at :15-25 replaces the rule's options for all **/*.js) / delta every auth-internal import in src/ outside src/auth/
Baseline:     none; restoring the rule adds 1 existing violation (src/billing/invoice.js:1)
Status:       BLOCKING (for debugger statements only)
Decision:     RESTORE
Guard:        committed known-bad fixture run through the assembled config in CI, asserting the boundary message and a non-zero exit
Handoff:      architecture-as-code (boundary rule form, auth public API for billing)
Next action:  Move the boundary to no-restricted-imports in eslint.config.mjs and add the CI negative control in the same change
Verification: Not run — I only had read-only tools in this session; I didn't run `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js` or `npm run lint`
```
